stem: Your sister calls you from home to say her daughter, Georgia, is having a severe asthma attack. Georgia’s reliever medication is Ventolin, but the Asthma Action Plan is unavailable. How should you counsel your sister?

options.text: Give 4 puffs of Ventolin, wait 4 minutes, then give another 4 puffs
Give 4 puffs of Ventolin, wait 10 minutes, then give another 4 puffs
Give 6 puffs of Ventolin, wait 20 minutes, then give another 6 puffs
Give 6 puffs of Ventolin, wait 3 hours, then give another 6 puffs

explanation: In acute severe asthma, short-acting beta-agonist (e.g. salbutamol/Ventolin) is given promptly and repeated after 4 minutes if needed. Delayed repeat dosing is inappropriate in severe respiratory distress.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part B

rationale: Selected from the existing options because one option matches standard first-aid reliever advice for severe asthma.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: 4 puffs now, then repeat after 4 minutes if there is no improvement.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect: 10 minutes is too long to wait in severe asthma.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect: 6 puffs and a 20-minute delay do not match standard urgent reliever advice.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect: 3 hours is far too long in a rapidly deteriorating asthma attack.
